title: Committee of Supply − Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: Budget cut for Head U
sections.summary: A motion proposes reducing Head U of the Estimates by $100, citing rapid global change, Asian growth opportunities, intensifying competition, technological shifts and an ageing local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head U of the Estimates be reduced by $100." The global operating environment is evolving rapidly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: There are many growth opportunities in Asia, but economic competition is also intensifying and technological changes are reshaping competitive advantages across economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Domestically, we are faced with an ageing local workforce which can pose constraints on our growth.

sections.label: Public Service digital skills progress
sections.summary: It asks what progress the Public Service has made in upgrading public officers' digital skills, saying SkillsFuture should apply equally to the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In short, SkillsFuture should apply equally to the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: What is the progress of the Public Service in upgrading the digital skills of our public officers?

sections.label: Assisting officers with training
sections.summary: It asks how the Singapore Public Service helps officers with training, capabilities, software, technology adoption and managing mindsets for adaptation, alignment and buy-in.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How is the Singapore Public Service assisting the officers in providing adequate training, building of capabilities, acquisition of the necessary software, technology adoption as well as nurturing and managing the mindsets of officers to ensure adaptation, alignment and buy-in?

sections.label: Safe coordination and confidentiality
sections.summary: It asks how the Public Service will ensure safe coordination and integration of information, data and details across the service while maintaining confidentiality amid disruptions and interventions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: With the amount of disruptions and interventions that we face today, how will the Public Service ensure safe coordination and integration of information, data and details across the service whilst, at the same time, maintaining confidentiality?

sections.label: Whole-of-Government citizen-centric services
sections.summary: It states that agencies face declining citizen satisfaction and higher costs from repeated touchpoints, and calls for a coordinating unit sharing data across agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Government agencies, in turn, face both declining citizen satisfaction and also incur higher costs from repeated touchpoints across agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: A citizen-centric Government should function as an integral unit adopting a whole-of-Government approach when delivering services to citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This calls for a coordinating unit that cuts across silos like, Ministries, Statutory Boards and departments, and sharing data freely at the backend across all agencies.

sections.label: Steps to restore public confidence
sections.summary: It asks what specific steps the Government is taking to restore public confidence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What specific steps are being taken by the Government to restore public confidence?

sections.label: Public Service officers and constitutional appointments
sections.summary: The passage expresses appreciation for Public Service officers and cites constitutional roles of the Attorney-General and Auditor-General.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my clarifications, I want to take this opportunity to express my appreciation for every Public Service officer in the service who serves sincerely and wholeheartedly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These appointments are recommended by the Prime Minister and subject to the discretionary approval of the President.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under Article 35, the Attorney-General shall have power, exercisable at his discretion, to institute, conduct or discontinue any proceedings for any offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Another example is the Auditor-General, who, under Article 148(F) is entrusted with the constitutional duty to audit and report on the accounts of all departments and offices of the Government, the Public Service Commission, the Legal Service Commission, the Supreme Court or Subordinate Courts and Parliament.

sections.label: Appointee spouse of Senior Minister of State
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Prime Minister to confirm the appointee is a Senior Minister of State's spouse and whether independence perception was considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Indeed, I am prepared to assume that she will do her best to do her work honourably.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, can the Prime Minister confirm that the current appointee is the spouse of a Senior Minister of State?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And if this is so, did the Prime Minister consider how appointing the spouse of a Senior Minister of State would affect the public perception of the independence of the AGO?

sections.label: CSC partners Institutes of Higher Learning
sections.summary: The CSC announced partnering 12 Institutes of Higher Learning to support public sector transformation and give officers one digital learning platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Last year, the CSC announced that it is partnering the 12 Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to support public sector transformation, as well as the transformation of learning within the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Public officers will have access to one digital learning platform.

sections.label: Progression pegged to on-the-job performance
sections.summary: Officer progression is pegged to on-the-job performance rather than educational qualification, done for MOE, Management Executive Scheme and Air Traffic Control Officer Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Beyond the point of recruitment, an officer's progression is pegged to their on-the-job performance rather than their educational qualification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This has been done for the Ministry of Education (MOE), the generic Management Executive Scheme in the Civil Service, and the Air Traffic Control Officer Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Minister Ong Ye Kung indicated that PSD will work with other public agencies to identify more areas where this can be implemented.

sections.label: Designing services around people and issues
sections.summary: The Public Service will design services around people and issues, with the Moments of Life app as an example of new ways of serving citizens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Public Service will progressively approach the design of many of our services around people and issues, rather than just expect people to adjust to our existing structures and ways of working.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Moments of Life app for families, launched last June, is a small example of how the Public Service can come up with new ways of serving citizens better, by working with citizens and the private sector, as partners.

sections.label: Moments of Life app for families
sections.summary: The app lets parents register a birth, apply for Baby Bonus and child library membership at once, and has been downloaded over 20,000 times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The outcome was an app that allows parents to register their child’s birth, apply for Baby Bonus and child library membership, all at one go.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: They do not need to approach multiple agencies and produce the same physical documents for verification again and again.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This app has been downloaded over 20,000 times in less than a year and I am happy to say that, beyond public hospitals, we have begun offering this service at private hospitals, starting with Thomson Medical Centre earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Other private hospitals will progressively come on board in the coming months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It has since started more projects to redesign services around more key moments, including pregnancy, parenting a school-going child, National Service, and entering one's silver years.

sections.label: Agencies co-locate and cross-train staff
sections.summary: Six agencies are co-locating and cross-training counter staff so each can provide about 70 services across the agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It started by co-locating different agencies together to serve citizens in one physical location.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This year, the six agencies are coming together to cross-train counter staff, and each staff will be able to provide a range of some 70 services across the six Government agencies.

sections.label: SSOs pilot job help
sections.summary: SSOs at five locations are piloting having the same officer who gives financial assistance also help residents find jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For instance, the SSOs at Taman Jurong, Kreta Ayer, Yishun, Chua Chu Kang and Jalan Besar are piloting an effort for the same SSO officer who provides financial assistance to unemployed residents to also help them find jobs.

sections.label: Engagement Immersion for Leaders launched
sections.summary: PSD and MCCY launched a new Engagement Immersion for Leaders programme last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: PSD and the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) launched a new Engagement Immersion for Leaders programme last year.

sections.label: Officers sent on company attachments
sections.summary: Ten officers were sent for attachments to companies including DBS, Singtel and Grab through the inaugural Service Delivery Talent Attachment Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For example, we sent 10 officers for attachments to various companies, such as the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS), Singtel and Grab, through the inaugural Service Delivery Talent Attachment Programme last year.

sections.label: Public Service digital literacy aim
sections.summary: The Public Service is aiming for 100% digital literacy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Public Service is aiming for 100% digital literacy.

sections.label: Platform accounts and courses completed
sections.summary: In the three months since launch, over 34,000 accounts were activated and almost 10,000 courses completed on the platform.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In the last three months since the launch, over 34,000 accounts have been activated and almost 10,000 courses have been completed on this platform.

sections.label: Future Public Service leadership criteria
sections.summary: The Public Service will increasingly seek operations, communications, mobilisation and international exposure, beyond pure policymaking skills, when selecting future leadership teams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Going forward, when our Public Service selects future leadership teams, we will increasingly look for a combination of operations, communications, mobilisation and international exposure, beyond pure policymaking skills.

sections.label: Merging of Public Service salary schemes
sections.summary: Since 2015, the Public Service has been merging salary schemes so ITE graduates, diploma and degree holders are recruited and progressed on the same structure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Since 2015, the Public Service has been merging salary schemes such that the ITE graduates, diploma and degree holders are recruited and progressed on the same structure.

sections.label: EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement coordination
sections.summary: The recently concluded EUSFTA was planned almost a decade ago and achieved through close coordination among many agencies, including MTI, AGC, MinLaw, IPOS, MOM and MEWR.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The recently concluded European Union (EU)-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (EUSFTA) was planned almost a decade ago and was achieved through close coordination among many agencies, including the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC), the Ministry of Law (MinLaw), the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS), the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources (MEWR).

sections.label: Tuas Terminal completion timeline
sections.summary: The proposed new Tuas Terminal is already taking shape and will be progressively completed by the 2040s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Today, the proposed new Tuas Terminal is already taking shape and will be progressively completed by the 2040s.

sections.label: Sylvia Lim on constitutional appointment criteria
sections.summary: Ms Sylvia Lim asked for clarification on the selection process and criteria used by the Prime Minister in identifying persons to fill key constitutional appointments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked for clarification on the selection process and criteria used by the Prime Minister in identifying persons to fill key constitutional appointments.

sections.label: Auditor-General appointment and consultation process
sections.summary: Ms Sylvia Lim asked if they are aware the new Auditor-General, Ms Goh Soon Poh, is the wife of Senior Minister of State Mr Heng Chee How; the Auditor-General is appointed by the President on the Prime Minister's advice, and the candidate was proposed to the President after consulting the Chairman of the Public Service Commission.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked if we are aware that Ms Goh Soon Poh, the new Auditor-General, is the wife of Senior Minister of State Mr Heng Chee How.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Auditor-General is appointed by the President in accordance with the advice of the Prime Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The candidate was proposed to the President for his concurrence after consulting the Chairman of the Public Service Commission.

sections.label: Pensioners covered under MediShield Life
sections.summary: Government pensioners have been covered under MediShield Life since 1 November 2015, like all Citizens and Permanent Residents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Like all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, Government pensioners have been covered under MediShield Life from 1 November 2015.

sections.label: Public Service and low birth rates
sections.summary: The speaker is confident Singapore can prevail if citizens unite, and notes birth rates remain low as the population ages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If we put our hearts, minds and hands together as one Singapore team, I am confident that we can prevail against the challenges and Singapore will remain vibrant and successful.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our Public Service will lead and support fellow Singaporeans in achieving this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, despite a comprehensive strategy to encourage Singaporeans to marry and have children, our birth rates remain low as our population continues to age.

sections.label: Women taking years off work
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a more radical system was looked into for women with children to take three to six years off work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Have we looked into a more radical or new system whereby women with children may take three to six years off the workforce to bring up their children?

sections.label: Grandchildren caregiver allowance for seniors
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a grandchildren caregiver allowance for seniors looking after their grandchildren can be looked into.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Similar to the proposed caregiver allowance for seniors, can we look into a grandchildren caregiver allowance for seniors looking after their grandchildren?

sections.label: Upper limit for immigration
sections.summary: The passage asks what upper limit is set for immigration so as not to affect the social compact.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What is the upper limit we set for immigration so as not to affect our social compact ?

sections.label: Low TFR and future DNA
sections.summary: The passage states that with a low TFR of 1.16, one of the world's lowest, the future of our DNA is at risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, with our low TFR at 1.16, one of the lowest rates in the world, the future of our DNA is at risk.

sections.label: Singapore TFR decline
sections.summary: Singapore's TFR rose in 2015 but has since dropped to an all-time low of 1.16 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, in 2015, we had a bumper year in terms of babies in Singapore and a rise in our TFR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, since then, Singapore's TFR seems to have dropped to an all-time low of 1.16 in 2018.

sections.label: Low TFR and intentions
sections.summary: In 2017 the TFR was 1.16, a seven-year low, despite billions spent and over 80% of young Singaporeans intending to marry and have children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In 2017, our TFR was a dismal 1.16.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It was a seven-year low and the second lowest on record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is despite the billions that we have committed to promoting marriage and parenthood over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Surveys tell us that over 80% of young Singaporeans intend to get married and have children, but that intention seems not to be reflected in the actual numbers getting married and also having children.

sections.label: Work culture and family
sections.summary: A purely transactional relationship causes stress, so work culture must change beyond incentives like the Enhanced Work-Life Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A purely transactional relationship only engenders stress, where parents fear even taking time off for family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We need to do more to encourage a change in work culture and not just through incentives like the Enhanced Work-Life Grant.

sections.label: Public Service family care leave
sections.summary: The Government is asked to let the Public Service lead in providing family care leave, with infant care and childcare fees and subsidies cited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider having the Public Service to take the lead in providing family care leave for all public servants as a start?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Couples are spending, on average, $1,495 on full-day infant care monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Those who qualify for $600 subsidy still need to fork out about $900 a month for infant care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Similarly, Singapore Citizens are eligible for a basic subsidy of up to $300 for childcare per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Since 2001, the childcare operators have raised their median fees by 22%.

sections.label: Childcare and infant care leave
sections.summary: The current six days of childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave are insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The current six days of childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave are insufficient.

sections.label: Per-child childcare leave
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to consider per-child childcare leave and letting parents use sick leave when their child is sick.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can we consider giving childcare leave on a per child basis?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: For parents with two or more kids, can the Minister also consider allowing parents to use their sick leave entitlements also when their child is sick?

sections.label: Unpaid leave for parents of multiples
sections.summary: A Tripartite Standard was announced to encourage employers to give four weeks of unpaid leave for parents of multiples or preterm babies, and the Minister is asked for an update.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: It is an experience that I hope no parent has to go through and I hope that, through my sharing, our policies will change and they are changing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: It was announced last year that we will introduce a Tripartite Standard to encourage employers to provide four weeks of unpaid leave for parents of multiples or preterm babies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on how many employers are providing this leave?

sections.label: Average citizen births
sections.summary: The average number of citizen births in the last five years is higher than previous five-year periods, averaging 33,000 annually from 2014 to 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The average number of citizen births in the last five years is higher than the previous five-year periods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From 2014 to 2018, the average was 33,000 citizen births annually.

sections.label: Citizen babies born overseas
sections.summary: About 1,500 citizen babies born overseas were welcomed annually over the past five years, as many Singaporeans live overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: On top of this, many Singaporeans are living overseas, so we welcomed about 1,500 citizen babies born overseas annually over the past five years.

sections.label: Marriage and parenthood survey findings
sections.summary: The 2016 survey found most single millennials intended to marry and most married couples wanted two or more children, which may explain recent TFR drops.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From our 2016 Marriage and Parenthood Survey, more than eight in 10 single millennials indicated they intended to marry, and more than nine in 10 married couples said they wanted two or more children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The surge in the number of young Singaporeans entering the prime child-bearing age may be followed by a surge in births, but at a later stage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We believe this explains recent drops in Singapore's TFR to 1.16 in 2017 and 1.14 last year.

sections.label: Shorter waiting time flats and grants
sections.summary: Flats with shorter waiting times of about two to three years are available, and resale flat buyers can receive up to $120,000 in housing grants.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Flats with shorter waiting times – about two to three years, compared to three to four years for typical Build-To-Order flats – are now available to them.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The first batch was launched in November 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Those who may have urgent housing needs or location preferences, can choose to buy a resale flat and receive up to $120,000 in housing grants, which is $40,000 more than what a couple would have received in 2014.

sections.label: Support at first child's birth
sections.summary: When their first child is born, parents receive up to $18,000 through the MediSave Grant for Newborns, Baby Bonus Cash Gift, and Child Development Account.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When their first child is born, they receive up to $18,000 through the MediSave Grant for Newborns, Baby Bonus Cash Gift, and the Child Development Account (CDA).

sections.label: Paternity leave take-up increase
sections.summary: Fathers can now get up to eight weeks of leave in a child's first year, and paternity leave take-up rose from 37% in 2014 to 53% for recent cohorts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With up to eight weeks of leave, a father now has access to double the amount of leave in his child’s first year, compared to just five years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The take-up of Paternity Leave has been encouraging, increasing from 37% in 2014 to 53% for recent cohorts.

sections.label: South Korea fertility rate example
sections.summary: South Korea poured much resources to emulate the Nordic countries, but its TFR has not improved and fell to 0.98 last year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: South Korea, for example, poured much resources to emulate the Nordic countries.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But its TFR has not improved and fell to 0.98 last year.

sections.label: NPTD family formation consultation
sections.summary: The National Population and Talent Division will embark on a consultation process to listen to Singaporeans' needs and concerns around forming families.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the coming months, the National Population and Talent Division (NPTD) will embark on a consultation process to listen to the needs and concerns of Singaporeans around forming families, and how the Government and the community can better support their aspirations.

sections.label: Citizenships and PRs granted
sections.summary: Around 22,600 Singapore Citizenships were granted in 2018, including 1,600 to children born overseas, and 32,700 Permanent Residencies were granted.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Similar to the past few years, we granted around 22,600 Singapore Citizenships in 2018, of which 1,600 were to children born overseas to Singaporean parents.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With 32,700 Permanent Residencies granted last year, the Permanent Resident (PR) population remains stable at around 520,000.

sections.label: New citizens' family and work ties
sections.summary: One in four adults granted citizenship have family ties with Singaporeans, three in five lived in Singapore at least 10 years, and most are in younger working ages.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As a result, one in four adults granted citizenship in recent years have family ties with Singaporeans; three in five have lived in Singapore for at least 10 years; and the majority of our new citizens each year are in their younger and prime working ages.

sections.label: Life expectancy world ranking
sections.summary: Today, Singapore's life expectancy is the third highest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Today, our life expectancy is the third highest in the world.

sections.label: Healthcare schemes for seniors
sections.summary: The Government introduced CHAS, Silver Support, MediShield Life and CareShield Life, plus Pioneer and Merdeka Generation Packages, to help families care for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Beyond CPF Life, the Government also introduced the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), Silver Support, MediShield Life and now, CareShield Life, to help families take better care of their seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For older Singaporeans who may have less in MediSave, we have provided the Pioneer and Merdeka Generation Packages with a focus on keeping quality healthcare affordable to seniors.

sections.label: Marriage and citizen birth trends
sections.summary: Citizen births averaged 33,000 yearly from 2014 to 2018, higher than 31,400 from 2009 to 2013 and 32,000 from 2004 to 2008.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the last five years, trends in marriages and citizen births are encouraging.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There were on average 33,000 citizen births each year between 2014 and 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the earlier five-year periods, the annual average was lower, at 31,400 from 2009 to 2013 and 32,000 from 2004 to 2008.

sections.label: Smart Nation initiative launch
sections.summary: The Smart Nation initiative, launched in late 2014, applies digital and smart solutions and has pilot projects like contactless public transport payment and TeleHealth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Smart Nation initiative was launched in late 2014 with the aim of applying digital and smart solutions to provide better services to our residents and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Since its inception, the Smart Nation Initiative has gone on to embark on numerous pilot projects and trials, some of which, like contactless payment for public transport and TeleHealth, are starting to bear fruit.

sections.label: Estonia's X-Road benefits
sections.summary: Estonia's government use of X-Road benefits citizens and builds trust, saving over 820 years of working time annually for the state and citizens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In Estonia, the use of X-Road by its government offered much benefit to its citizens making life easier at every level and at engendering support for and trust towards its smart government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It is estimated that X-Road saves more than 820 years of working time for the state and its citizens annually.

sections.label: Digital Defence sixth pillar
sections.summary: Digital Defence is now the sixth pillar of Total Defence, and all, including the Government, play a role in it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Digital Defence is now our sixth pillar of Total Defence, and all, including the Government, play a role in this.

sections.label: Annual cybersecurity readiness report proposal
sections.summary: Given risks and breaches, the question asks whether the Government would publish an annual report on public agencies' cybersecurity readiness to reassure citizens and encourage high standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: In view of the risks and breaches that had occurred, would the Government look into publishing an annual report on the cybersecurity readiness of public agencies to give some reassurance to citizens and to encourage the achievement of high standards?

sections.label: Moments of Life application
sections.summary: Moments of Life is a one-stop application letting new parents register a birth and apply for Baby Bonus in a single application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: The Moments of Life initiative is a good example – a one-stop application to help Singaporeans navigate the journey of welcoming a newborn and raise a young child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
